q: A stores official has to look up, in the Indian Railway Stores Code, both the rules for purchase of stores and the rules for depot working, custody and accounts of stores. He finds that the Code:

options.A: Is issued in a single volume dealing only with purchase of stores
options.B: Is issued in two volumes, Volume I dealing mainly with purchase of stores and Volume II with depot working, custody and accounts of stores
options.C: Is issued in three volumes, one for each stores depot
options.D: Contains no rules for depot working or custody of stores

e: The Indian Railway Stores Code is issued in two volumes - Volume I deals mainly with purchase of stores and Volume II with depot working, custody and accounts of stores.

q: A depot officer questions the authority behind the rules in the Stores Code. The Indian Railway Stores Code, containing the rules for the purchase, custody, accounting and disposal of stores, is issued by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation

e: The Stores Code containing rules for purchase, custody, accounting and disposal of stores is issued by the Railway Board, the apex authority for railway stores matters.

q: A purchase clerk allots a Price Ledger number to an item stocked in a depot for the first time. In the codification in force on the Railways, the number so allotted runs to:
e: Under the codification in force on Indian Railways, each stocked item is allotted an 8-digit Price Ledger (PL) number for uniform identification across depots.

q: While the Stores Budget of a railway is being framed, the value of the stores which the railway expects to purchase and receive during the year is entered in the budget as its anticipated:

options.C: Closing balance at the end of the year

e: In the Stores Budget, anticipated receipts - the value of stores expected to be purchased and received during the year - are shown as anticipated debits to the stock account.

q: At the close of a half year, the Stores Accounts office prepares a statement showing the balances of stores under the stock and suspense heads and proving that the priced ledger agrees with the general books. That statement is the:

options.A: Half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts
options.D: Works Register of the Stores Department

e: The Half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts shows balances under stock and suspense heads and proves agreement between the priced ledger and the general books.

q: Stores are issued from a depot to another railway and the value of the issue awaits final adjustment and recovery. Until that adjustment is made, the value is held in the stores accounts under:
e: Issues to other railways awaiting final adjustment and recovery are held under Stores Miscellaneous Suspense in the stores accounts until adjustment is completed.

q: A field official holding imprest stores has consumed a part of them on works and renders his account of the consumption. His imprest stores are replenished:

options.A: Only after a fresh tender is invited for the quantity consumed
options.B: Only against the annual budget allotment of his office
options.C: On the basis of the account of consumption rendered by him
options.D: On the basis of a narrative report of the Stock Verifier

e: Imprest stores held by field officials are replenished on the basis of the account of consumption rendered by the holder, as per the Stores Code imprest rules.

q: Spanners, hammers and similar tools issued to a work gang remain the property of the Railway and have to be accounted for numerically by the official holding them. In the records of the department, such tools and plant are borne on the:
e: Tools and plant such as spanners and hammers remain railway property and are accounted for numerically in the Dead Stock Register of the holding official, not in the priced ledger.

q: A stock sheet received in a headquarters office is signed with the initials 'ASV' of the Accounts official who verified the stock. In the Accounts Department, 'ASV' stands for:
e: In the Accounts Department, ASV stands for Assistant Stock Verifier, the official who verifies stock and signs stock sheets in that capacity.

q: The receipt notes, issue notes, bin cards and stock sheets used in a stores depot are printed forms belonging to a particular series of Indian Railway standard forms. That series is the:
e: Receipt notes, issue notes, bin cards and stock sheets are Indian Railway standard forms of the S-series, the series prescribed for stores forms.

q: Tenders for a stores item have just been opened and the case has to be put up to the Tender Committee for its recommendations. Before the case is so put up, the purchase office first prepares:

options.A: A comparative statement (tabulation) of the offers received
options.B: A purchase order in favour of the lowest tenderer
options.C: A receipt note for the stores tendered for
options.D: A stock sheet for the item tendered for

e: Before a tender case is put up to the Tender Committee, the purchase office prepares a comparative statement (tabulation) of all offers received, as required by purchase procedure.

q: After a purchase order has been placed, a change in the rate in the order becomes necessary, which increases the total value of the order. An amendment of this kind, having financial implications, can be issued:

options.A: By the depot storekeeper on his own authority
options.B: Orally by the purchase clerk dealing with the case
options.C: As a routine correction, without any approval
options.D: Only with the concurrence of Finance

e: An amendment to a purchase order that increases its total value has financial implications and can be issued only with the concurrence of Finance.

q: In a tender covered by the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a Class-I local supplier is entitled to purchase preference over the lowest bid within a prescribed margin. That margin of purchase preference is:
e: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a Class-I local supplier gets purchase preference over L1 within a margin of 20 percent.

q: For a stores purchase in which inspection is prescribed, the Railway does not carry out the inspection through its own staff but entrusts it to an outside agency acting on its behalf. Such inspection on behalf of the Railways may be carried out by:

options.A: RITES, acting as an inspection agency
options.B: The supplier's own staff, without any independent check
options.C: The Accounts stock verifiers of the depot

e: Where inspection is entrusted to an outside agency on behalf of the Railways, it may be carried out by RITES acting as an inspection agency.

q: A purchase order placed on a firm names the depot which is to receive the material supplied against the order and account for its receipt. In the purchase order, that depot/official is referred to as the:
e: The depot or official named in the purchase order to receive the material and account for its receipt is the consignee.

q: A bill for goods purchased through the Government e-Marketplace is not passed on paper in the ordinary way; it is processed through the GeM portal itself. For this processing, the GeM portal is linked with the Railways':
e: Bills for GeM purchases are processed through the GeM portal linked with IPAS, the Railways integrated payroll and accounting system, for payment.

q: While framing the conditions of a high-value stores tender, the purchase office works out the earnest money to be taken from the tenderers. Whatever the value of the tender, the Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender cannot exceed:
e: As per stores tender conditions, Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender cannot exceed Rs 50 lakh, whatever the value of the tender.

q: Material is received into a stores depot at the start of the accounting chain, before it is issued to any consuming department or work. In the General Books of the railway, such receipts of stores are, in the first instance, accounted for under:

options.A: The final revenue heads of the consuming departments

e: Receipts of stores are first accounted for in the General Books under Stores Suspense (the stock account), and charged to final heads only on issue.

q: A supplier offering stores under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order declares that the local content in the item offered by him is 35 per cent. On that declaration, the supplier is classified as a:
e: Under the Make in India Order, local content of 20 percent to 50 percent makes a supplier a Class-II local supplier; 35 percent therefore falls in Class-II, Class-I requiring 50 percent or more.

q: For an important imported machine, a depot stocks an expensive spare which may remain without any issue for years, only to guard against a prolonged breakdown of the machine. Such a costly, slow-moving spare is known in stores parlance as:
e: A costly spare stocked to guard against prolonged breakdown of an important machine, though it may lie unissued for years, is an insurance spare.

q: An old office order in a zonal railway addresses the head of its stores organisation as the Controller of Stores. The present designation of the head of the stores organisation at the headquarters of a zonal railway is:
e: The head of the stores organisation at zonal railway headquarters is now designated Principal Chief Materials Manager (PCMM), earlier called Controller of Stores.

q: At the close of the year, an assistant proposes to charge depreciation on the stores lying in the depots of the railway, as is done for its plant and buildings. The correct position is that depreciation is not charged on:

options.A: Plant and machinery installed in workshops
options.B: Stores held in stock in depots, which are current assets valued at book (cost) value
options.C: Rolling stock owned by the Railways
options.D: Buildings and structures of the Railways

e: Depreciation is not charged on stores held in stock in depots, because they are current assets valued at book (cost) value, unlike plant, buildings and rolling stock.

q: A Government buyer who goes to the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to procure common-use goods and services finds that the portal provides more than one mode of buying. The modes available to a buyer on GeM are:

options.D: Direct purchase, bidding and reverse auction

e: GeM offers buyers three modes of procurement for common-use goods and services - direct purchase, bidding and reverse auction - under GFR provisions for GeM.

q: A tender notice for stores records that firms registered with the NSIC are exempted from payment of Earnest Money Deposit. The full name of the NSIC is:
e: NSIC stands for National Small Industries Corporation; firms registered with it are exempted from Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders as per tender conditions.

q: Soon after a purchase order for an item is completed, the same item is required again, and an order is placed on the same supplier at the same rates and on the same terms as the recent order, instead of a fresh tender being invited. Such an order placed on the same supplier is known as a:
e: An order placed on the same supplier at the same rates and terms as a recent completed order, without a fresh tender, is a repeat order.

q: A supplier despatches a wagon load of stores to a depot. So that the depot can claim and take delivery of the consignment when the wagon arrives, the document which the supplier forwards to the consignee depot for that purpose is the:
e: The supplier forwards the Railway Receipt (RR) to the consignee depot so that the depot can claim and take delivery of the wagon consignment on arrival.

q: Diesel locomotives running on a section draw their High Speed Diesel from the Railways' own fuel installations provided for the purpose. Those fuel installations are known as:

options.B: Imprest stores held by loco pilots
options.C: Oil sidings of the Traffic Department

e: Railway Consumer Depots (RCDs) are the Railways own fuel installations from which diesel locomotives draw High Speed Diesel.

q: At the Economic Order Quantity of a stores item, the annual ordering cost and the annual inventory carrying cost of the item are:
e: At the Economic Order Quantity, annual ordering cost equals annual inventory carrying cost, and total cost is minimum at this balance point.

q: Consider the following statements about stores imported on 'F.O.B.' (Free On Board) terms: 1. The marine insurance of the consignment for the sea transit is arranged by the Railway, as buyer, since the price does not cover insurance beyond the port of shipment. 2. The price covers cost, insurance and freight up to the destination port in India. Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: On F.O.B. terms the price covers cost and freight to the shipment port only, so marine insurance for sea transit is arranged by the buyer Railway - statement 1 only is correct; cost, insurance and freight to destination describes C.I.F. terms.

q: Stores rejected on inspection at a depot are removed from the depot by:

options.A: The Railway, at its own cost in all cases
options.B: The depot storekeeper, at his personal cost
options.C: The purchaser of scrap in the next e-auction
options.D: The supplier, at his own cost within the period stipulated in the contract

e: Stores rejected on inspection must be removed by the supplier at his own cost within the period stipulated in the contract, as per the GCC for supply.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of an item is found in one ward of a depot and an excess of the same item is found in another ward of the same depot. The correct treatment is that:

options.A: The shortage is set off against the excess and no stock sheet is prepared
options.B: Only the shortage is brought on record, the excess being ignored
options.C: Each difference is brought on record and adjusted separately through its own stock sheet; the one is not set off against the other
options.D: Both differences are recovered in cash from the two stockholders jointly

e: Each shortage or excess found on stock verification is recorded and adjusted separately through its own stock sheet; a shortage in one ward is not set off against an excess in another.

q: A firm's tender for stores has been accepted and the letter of acceptance of the tender has been issued to it. The firm is required to furnish the Security Deposit under the contract:

options.A: Within 7 days of the opening of tenders
options.C: Within 21 days of the issue of the letter of acceptance of the tender
options.D: Only after the supplies are completed

e: Under the GCC for supply, the successful tenderer must furnish Security Deposit within 21 days of the issue of the letter of acceptance of the tender.

q: A depot succeeds in reducing the clerical, tendering and progressing cost incurred in placing each order for an item, the other costs remaining unchanged. Other things remaining the same, the Economic Order Quantity of the item will:

options.D: Become equal to the annual consumption

e: EOQ varies with the square root of ordering cost; reducing the cost of placing each order therefore decreases the Economic Order Quantity.

q: A trainee in a purchase office lists the stages through which a stores requirement passes, from the demand to the order on the supplier. The correct sequence of those stages is:

options.A: Purchase Order, Tender, Indent, Tender Committee recommendations
options.B: Indent/Demand, Invitation of tenders, Tender Committee recommendations, Acceptance, Purchase Order
options.C: Tender Committee recommendations, Indent, Purchase Order, Invitation of tenders
options.D: Acceptance, Indent, Purchase Order, Invitation of tenders

e: The purchase sequence is Indent/Demand, invitation of tenders, Tender Committee recommendations, acceptance, and then the Purchase Order.

q: Two deposits figure in a stores tender. The deposit which every tenderer furnishes along with his tender itself, as distinct from the deposit furnished later by the successful tenderer after acceptance of his tender, is the:
e: The deposit furnished by every tenderer along with his tender is the Earnest Money Deposit; Security Deposit and Performance Security are furnished later by the successful tenderer.

q: Consider the following statements about stores accounting in the General Books: 1. Issues of stores from depots are credited to the Stores Suspense (stock) account, the head of account of the consuming department or work being debited with their value. 2. Issues of stores from depots are debited to the Stores Suspense (stock) account and credited to the head of the consuming department. Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Issues from depots are credited to Stores Suspense (stock) and debited to the head of the consuming department or work - statement 1 only is correct; statement 2 reverses the entries.

q: A bidder is the successful (highest) bidder for a lot of scrap in an e-auction and proceeds to pay the sale value of the lot. The earnest money deposited by him for the lot is dealt with by:

options.A: Refunding it to him immediately after the auction in all cases
options.B: Forfeiting it to the Railway in all cases
options.C: Crediting it to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Adjusting it towards the sale value payable by him for the lot

e: The earnest money of the successful highest bidder in a scrap e-auction is adjusted towards the sale value payable by him for the lot, as per conditions of sale.

q: The total issues of stores of a railway during a year are Rs 4.8 crore and the average stock held is Rs 80 lakh. The stock of stores turns over, i.e. the inventory turnover, during the year is:
e: Inventory turnover = total issues / average stock = Rs 4.8 crore / Rs 80 lakh = 480 / 80 = 6 times.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 12,600 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 900 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / EOQ = 12,600 / 900 = 14 orders.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 750 units and a safety stock of 250 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the maximum inventory of the item will be:
e: Maximum inventory = EOQ + safety stock = 750 + 250 = 1,000 units, reached when a fresh consignment arrives.

q: The average consumption of an item is 90 units per week. Its average lead time is 4 weeks, but the lead time may extend up to 7 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided against lead-time variation is:
e: Safety stock = average consumption x (maximum lead time - average lead time) = 90 x (7 - 4) = 270 units.

q: A depot holds an opening stock of 1,600 units of an item. During the year, 800 units are received into stock and 1,900 units are issued. The book rate of the item is Rs 45 per unit. The value of the closing stock of the item is:
e: Closing quantity = 1,600 + 800 - 1,900 = 500 units; value = 500 x Rs 45 = Rs 22,500.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 25 per unit. Fresh receipts of 200 units at Rs 40 per unit and 200 units at Rs 48 per unit are taken into stock. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

During a month, stores bills amounting to Rs 32 lakh were paid and accounted for under Purchase Suspense, and material worth Rs 27 lakh was received at the depots and linked with the bills during the same month. The net amount added to the debit balance under Purchase Suspense during the month is:
e: Net addition to Purchase Suspense debit = bills paid minus material received and linked = Rs 32 lakh - Rs 27 lakh = Rs 5 lakh.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 45 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 3.6 crore. The stock held in the depots represents, broadly, issues for a period of:
e: Months of issues held = closing balance / annual issues x 12 = 45 / 360 x 12 = 1.5 months.

q: A wagon consignment of stores is opened at a depot and a part of the material is found short and another part damaged in transit. The correct course for the depot is to:

options.A: Accept the consignment silently and bear the shortage as a normal depot loss
options.B: Record the shortage and damage on the receipt documents and prefer a claim on the supplier or the carrier, as the case may be
options.C: Refuse delivery of the entire consignment in every such case
options.D: Recover the value of the shortage from the pay of the storekeeper receiving the wagon

e: Shortage or damage in transit must be recorded on the receipt documents and a claim preferred on the supplier or the carrier, as applicable, instead of being silently borne by the depot.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 72 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 4.8 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 72 lakh / Rs 4.8 crore = 72 / 480 = 0.15.

q: Material has arrived at a depot against a purchase order but its inspection is still pending. Until the inspection is completed, the material is taken into the priced stock accounts of the depot:

options.A: Immediately on its arrival at the depot gate
options.B: On the date the purchase order was placed
options.C: At the close of the month of its arrival in all cases
options.D: Only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued

e: Material is taken into priced stock only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued, as per Stores Code receipt procedure.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 7,200 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 2 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 7,200 x 50 / 2) = square root of 3,60,000 = 600 units.

q: Stores are despatched by one depot to another depot of the same railway under a transfer advice, but the receiving depot has not yet acknowledged their receipt. In the accounts, the stores continue to remain on the books of:

options.A: Neither depot, the stores going out of account during transit
options.B: The despatching depot, until their receipt is acknowledged by the receiving depot
options.C: The headquarters purchase office which arranged the transfer
options.D: The Traffic Accounts office, as a traffic suspense item

e: Stores despatched on transfer remain on the books of the despatching depot until the receiving depot acknowledges their receipt.

q: A depot holds 500 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 30 per unit. A fresh receipt of 300 units is taken into stock at Rs 46 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Total value = (500 x 30) + (300 x 46) = 15,000 + 13,800 = Rs 28,800 for 800 units, so revised rate = 28,800 / 800 = Rs 36 per unit.

q: A mixed lot of stores released from a completed work is returned to a depot. After the returned material has been examined, it is classified, according to its condition, as:

options.B: Stock or non-stock, according to the source of its purchase
options.C: Imported or indigenous, according to its origin
options.D: A-category or C-category, according to its value alone

e: Material returned from a completed work is examined and classified by condition as re-usable (serviceable), repairable, or scrap, before disposal or re-stocking.

q: The AAC of an item is 4,800 units. The stock in hand is 900 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 4,800 / 12 = 400 units; coverage = (stock + dues) / monthly consumption = (900 + 300) / 400 = 3 months.

q: A component manufactured in a railway workshop is transferred to a stores depot for stocking. The value at which the depot takes the component into stock is:

options.A: The prevailing market price of a similar component
options.B: The cost of the raw material consumed alone
options.C: The cost of manufacture, comprising material, labour and on-cost, as worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: A nominal value fixed by the depot officer

e: A workshop-manufactured component is taken into depot stock at its cost of manufacture - material, labour and on-cost - worked out through Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: The average consumption of an item is 120 units per week, the lead time is 6 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 280 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = (average consumption x lead time) + safety stock = (120 x 6) + 280 = 720 + 280 = 1,000 units.

q: An imported consignment is covered by a Letter of Credit opened by the Railway. Under the Letter of Credit, payment to the foreign supplier is made:

options.A: Against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, and not on the physical receipt of the material in India
options.B: Only after the material has been received and verified in the Indian depot
options.C: In cash to the supplier's agent when the ship reaches the Indian port
options.D: Only after the depot issues the material to a consuming department

e: Under a Letter of Credit, the foreign supplier is paid by the bank against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents, not on physical receipt of material in India.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 4,50,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 6 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear per week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 percent per week x 6 weeks x Rs 4,50,000 = 3 percent x 4,50,000 = Rs 13,500.

q: The net balance accumulated in the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway during a year is finally cleared:

options.A: By carrying it forward indefinitely from year to year
options.B: By transfer to the Sales Suspense Account
options.C: At the close of the year, under the sanction of the competent authority
options.D: By adjustment against the salary bills of the depot staff

e: The net balance in the Stock Adjustment Account is cleared at the close of the year under the sanction of the competent authority, as per Stores Code provisions.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 7,25,000. The advance payment admissible at 98% of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 percent of Rs 7,25,000 = 0.98 x 7,25,000 = Rs 7,10,500, payable against inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: A trainee asks who is responsible for maintaining the Priced Stores Ledger of a depot, in which quantities as well as values of stores transactions are recorded. The ledger is maintained by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper who holds the stores in his custody
options.B: The purchase office which placed the orders for the stores
options.C: The consuming department which draws the stores
options.D: The Stores Accounts office of the Accounts Department

e: The Priced Stores Ledger, recording quantities and values, is maintained by the Stores Accounts office of the Accounts Department, separate from the custodian.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 14 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 46 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 51 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 9 lakh
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 19 lakh
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 5 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 5 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit + bills paid - material received and linked = 14 + 46 - 51 = Rs 9 lakh debit balance.

q: A purchase section works out the total lead time for procuring a stock item, from the raising of the demand to the receipt of the material. The total lead time so worked out comprises:

options.A: Only the delivery period allowed to the supplier in the purchase order
options.B: Only the time taken in inspection of the material after its receipt
options.C: The internal time taken in processing the demand and placing the order, plus the supplier's delivery period
options.D: The time for which the material thereafter remains in stock before issue

e: Total lead time comprises the internal time for processing the demand and placing the order plus the supplier delivery period, as per Stores Code provisioning.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,550 units. The average consumption is 95 units per week and the average lead time is 9 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,550 - (95 x 9) = 1,550 - 855 = 695 units.

q: The consumption trend of a stock item has changed materially since its AAC was last fixed. In regard to the AAC of such an item, the correct position is that the AAC is:

options.A: Reviewed periodically and revised, where necessary, in the light of the actual consumption trend of the item
options.B: Fixed once for all when the item is first stocked and never changed thereafter
options.C: Revised by the supplier of the item whenever he considers it necessary
options.D: Kept unchanged until the item is deleted from the Priced Vocabulary

e: AAC is reviewed periodically and revised where necessary in the light of the actual consumption trend; it is not fixed once for all.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,750 units and the re-order quantity is 1,150 units. The minimum consumption is 70 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,750 + 1,150 - (70 x 6) = 2,900 - 420 = 2,480 units.

q: A Government buyer needs a common-use article which is listed on the Government e-Marketplace, while a railway-specific stores item is to be procured by tender. GeM is distinguished from IREPS in that:

options.A: Both names refer to one and the same portal of the Railways
options.B: IREPS is the Railways' own e-procurement system for tenders, stores procurement and scrap e-auction, whereas GeM is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services
options.C: GeM is used by the Railways only for the sale of scrap
options.D: IREPS is the national marketplace on which all Government buyers purchase common-use goods

e: IREPS is the Railways own e-procurement system for tenders, stores procurement and scrap e-auction, whereas GeM is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services.

q: The average consumption of an item is 65 units per day and the lead time for emergency procurement is 4 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level = average consumption x lead time for emergency procurement = 65 x 4 = 260 units.

q: A consignment of imported stores has arrived at the Indian port of entry. The customs duty on the consignment is payable by the Railway:

options.A: Before the consignment is cleared through Customs at the port of entry
options.B: Only if the stores are later found defective and returned
options.C: One year after the date of import, without exception
options.D: By the foreign supplier in all cases, the Railway paying nothing

e: Customs duty on an imported consignment is payable by the Railway before the consignment is cleared through Customs at the port of entry.

q: The average consumption of an item is 85 units per week. Its average lead time is 5 weeks, but the lead time may extend up to 8 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided against this lead-time variation is:
e: Safety stock = average consumption x (maximum lead time - average lead time) = 85 x (8 - 5) = 255 units.

q: A firm registered with the Railways has, over a series of supplies, performed persistently poorly as a vendor. On the basis of its performance, the firm may face:

options.A: Automatic allotment of larger orders so that its performance improves
options.B: A fine imposed personally by the depot storekeeper
options.C: Down-gradation, suspension or cancellation of its registration
options.D: No consequence, registration once granted being irrevocable

e: A registered firm with persistently poor vendor performance may face down-gradation, suspension or cancellation of its registration under vendor approval rules.

q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 9,60,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit = 5 percent of Rs 9,60,000 = 0.05 x 9,60,000 = Rs 48,000.

q: An Accounts official is checking the book (issue) rate recorded in the Priced Stores Ledger for a purchased item. The book rate of such an item normally comprises:

options.A: The purchase price together with freight and other incidental charges incurred in bringing the material into stock
options.B: The purchase price alone, freight being recovered separately on every issue
options.C: The maximum retail price printed by the manufacturer of the item
options.D: The rate at which a similar item was last sold as scrap

e: The book rate of a purchased item normally comprises its purchase price together with freight and other incidental charges incurred in bringing it into stock.

q: A supplier fails to supply 650 units of stores contracted at Rs 72 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 95 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 95 - Rs 72) x 650 = Rs 23 x 650 = Rs 14,950, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Stock Adjustment Account adjusts differences in the quantity and value of stock. 2. Purchase Suspense bridges the gap between payment of bills and receipt of material, and vice versa. Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct - the Stock Adjustment Account adjusts quantity and value differences of stock, and Purchase Suspense bridges the gap between bill payment and material receipt, and vice versa.

q: Six wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 4 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,100 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 6 wagons x 4 days x Rs 1,100 per wagon per day = Rs 26,400.

q: A depot is covering a demand for the procurement of a stock item and has to decide the quantity to be ordered. That quantity is determined mainly with reference to:

options.A: The AAC (Average Annual Consumption) of the item and the prescribed period of coverage
options.B: The quantity ordered against the immediately preceding tender alone
options.C: The minimum order quantity insisted upon by the likely supplier
options.D: The balance physically seen in one bin of the depot on that day alone

e: The quantity to be ordered for a stock item is determined mainly with reference to its AAC and the prescribed period of coverage, after allowing for stock and dues.

q: A stores depot issues 725 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 44 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Value of issue = 725 units x Rs 44 per unit = Rs 31,900, debited to the consuming department at the book rate.

q: At the end of a month, each stores depot of a railway prepares a summary of its stores transactions for the month. The Stores Monthly Summary so prepared forms the basis for:

options.A: Fixing the pay of the depot staff for the month
options.B: Compilation of the stores accounts of the railway
options.C: Preparation of the catalogue for the next e-auction of scrap
options.D: Vetting of the AAC of A-category items by Headquarters Finance

e: The Stores Monthly Summary prepared by each depot forms the basis for compilation of the stores accounts of the railway.

q: A stores depot issues 300 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 80 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 10 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value = 300 x Rs 80 = Rs 24,000; with departmental charges at 10 percent, recoverable amount = 24,000 x 1.10 = Rs 26,400.

q: Balances have remained outstanding under the stores suspense heads of a railway for some months. In regard to such outstanding balances, the correct course is that they are:

options.A: Written off automatically at the end of every year without any linking
options.B: Transferred to the Capital account at the end of the year
options.C: Never reviewed once they have been booked under a suspense head
options.D: Reviewed periodically and cleared by linking them with the corresponding bills and adjustments

e: Outstanding balances under stores suspense heads must be reviewed periodically and cleared by linking them with the corresponding bills and adjustments.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 1.1 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 18 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 18 percent of Rs 1.1 crore = 0.18 x 1,10,00,000 = Rs 19,80,000.

q: The balances in the custody (bin) accounts of a depot do not agree with the balances in its priced accounts for certain items. The correct treatment of the disagreement is that the two sets of balances are:

options.A: Never compared with each other after the initial entries
options.B: Agreed with each other periodically, differences being investigated before they are adjusted
options.C: Agreed by altering the priced ledger to match the bin card without any enquiry
options.D: Compared only at the time the depot is closed down

e: Custody (bin) balances and priced balances are agreed periodically, and differences are investigated before any adjustment is made.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 9,900 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 900 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / EOQ = 9,900 / 900 = 11 orders.

q: Two depots of the same railway hold the same stock item, and a depot of another railway holds it as well. Under uniform pricing on a railway, the book (issue) rate of the item:

options.A: Is uniform within a railway, but may differ from one railway to another
options.B: Is fixed by the Railway Board uniformly for all railways
options.C: Differs from depot to depot within the same railway
options.D: Is the same on all the railways of Indian Railways

e: Under uniform pricing, the book (issue) rate of an item is uniform within a railway but may differ from one railway to another.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 840 units and a safety stock of 260 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the average inventory of the item held is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ / 2 + safety stock = 840 / 2 + 260 = 420 + 260 = 680 units.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 68 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.12 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.95 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening + receipts - issues = Rs 68 lakh + Rs 2.12 crore - Rs 1.95 crore = 68 + 212 - 195 = Rs 85 lakh.

q: The total issues of stores of a railway during a year are Rs 6.3 crore and the average stock held is Rs 90 lakh. The stock of stores turns over during the year:
e: Inventory turnover = total issues / average stock = Rs 6.3 crore / Rs 90 lakh = 630 / 90 = 7 times.

q: A depot holds an opening stock of 2,100 units of an item. During the year, 900 units are received into stock and 2,400 units are issued. The book rate of the item is Rs 55 per unit. The value of the closing stock of the item is:
e: Closing quantity = 2,100 + 900 - 2,400 = 600 units; value = 600 x Rs 55 = Rs 33,000.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,200 units. Coverage for five months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 650 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 450 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Quantity required for 5 months = (7,200 / 12) x 5 = 3,000 units; quantity to order = 3,000 - 650 stock - 450 dues = 1,900 units.

q: A depot holds 2,950 units of an item, whereas the maximum level fixed for the item is 2,400 units. The book rate of the item is Rs 52 per unit. The value of the stock held in excess of the maximum level is:
e: Excess over maximum = 2,950 - 2,400 = 550 units; value = 550 x Rs 52 = Rs 28,600.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 78 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 6.5 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 78 lakh / Rs 6.5 crore = 78 / 650 = 0.12.

q: Against a purchase order, a substantial part of the quantity has been supplied and accepted, but the balance quantity is no longer required and the purchase office closes the order without insisting on supply of that balance. The purchase order is then said to be:
e: A purchase order closed after part supply and acceptance, without insisting on the balance quantity no longer required, is said to be short-closed.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 12,100 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 12,100 x 50 / 4) = square root of 3,02,500 = 550 units.

q: A scrap lot is sold in an e-auction, but the purchaser defaults and the lot has to be put up for re-auction. The re-auction fetches less than the price at which the lot was originally sold. The shortfall in sale value is:

options.B: Recoverable from the defaulting purchaser, as per the conditions of sale
options.C: Written off without any recovery in all cases
options.D: Adjusted through the Purchase Suspense Account

e: On re-auction after a purchaser defaults, the shortfall in sale value is recoverable from the defaulting purchaser as per the conditions of sale.

q: A depot holds 850 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 28 per unit. A fresh receipt of 350 units is taken into stock at Rs 52 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Total value = (850 x 28) + (350 x 52) = 23,800 + 18,200 = Rs 42,000 for 1,200 units, so revised rate = 42,000 / 1,200 = Rs 35 per unit.

q: A custodian of stores detects a shortage of stores in his charge during the course of his own checks, well before the next stock verification falls due. As soon as the shortage is detected, he is required to:

options.A: Report the loss promptly to the controlling officer/Accounts, so that an enquiry into it can be ordered
options.B: Wait until the next annual stock verification before reporting it
options.C: Make good the loss quietly from his own pocket, without reporting it
options.D: Sell other surplus stores to cover up the shortage

e: A custodian detecting a shortage must report the loss promptly to the controlling officer and Accounts so that an enquiry can be ordered; it is not held over till stock verification.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,800 units. The stock in hand is 975 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 325 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 7,800 / 12 = 650 units; coverage = (975 + 325) / 650 = 1,300 / 650 = 2 months.

q: Stores are stolen from a depot and the custodian reports the theft to his departmental authorities. In addition to them, the matter is also reported to:

options.A: The firm which supplied the stores

e: Theft of stores must be reported, in addition to departmental authorities, to the RPF/Police for investigation.

q: The average consumption of an item is 155 units per week, the lead time is 6 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 370 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = (155 x 6) + 370 = 930 + 370 = 1,300 units.

q: A trainee asks on what assumption the Economic Order Quantity model rests. The model is based on the assumption that:

options.A: The consumption (demand) of the item is constant and known, and the ordering and carrying costs are known
options.B: The prices of the item rise every month
options.C: The lead time for supply is indefinite
options.D: Shortages of the item are permitted without any limit

e: The EOQ model assumes demand is constant and known and that ordering and carrying costs are known.
